correctness.rationale: Conjugation preserves the trace norm, so the translation cancels in differences and gives an exact isometry. The range is \(P+\mathcal C\). For \(X=B-P\), the support projection of \(X_-\) gives the lower bound \(\|X-C\|_1\ge\operatorname{Tr}X_-\) for every \(C\ge0\), and \(C=X_+\) attains it. The variational formula for \(\operatorname{Tr}X_-\) then bounds the pointwise distance by \(\operatorname{Tr}P\), while \(B=0\) attains that bound. Finally, evaluation at \(A=0\) gives the universal lower bound \(\operatorname{Tr}P\) on distance to any Wigner symmetry, and choosing the original \(U\) attains it. All quantifiers and boundary cases \(P=0\) and \(P\ne0\) are explicit.

originality.rationale: The focal 2026 paper proves stability for surjective maps and, under \(T(0)=0\), for finitely almost-surjective maps independently of the covering radius; it also gives proper-isometry embeddings showing that unrestricted nonsurjectivity is dangerous. Full-text inspection did not reveal the finite-covering-radius translated-cone identity or the equality between covering and Wigner defects. The closest positive-cone stability paper retains the standard normalization and does not state the trace-class translation boundary. Ten implication-level database queries and own-ledger comparisons found no covering result.

value.rationale: The result identifies a sharp and natural boundary for the focal stability theorem. It does more than exhibit a counterexample: it computes the entire point-to-range distance function for a canonical translated family and proves that two independently meaningful global defects--almost-surjectivity and distance from Wigner symmetry--coincide exactly. This shows quantitatively why fixing zero cannot be discarded from an error-only theorem and supplies the sharp coefficient \(1\) for any correction term proportional to covering radius on this family.
